entry.author: Whaikaha — Ministry of Disabled People
entry.summary:
Today (Tuesday 12 November 2024), the Prime Minister and senior public service officials apologised to survivors of abuse in care.

You can view the recording here: https://vimeo.com/1016895724/9e0ba34462

These apologies respond to the report from the Royal Commission of Inquiry into Abuse in Care of the State and Faith-based Institutions. This important report is called Whanaketia – Through Pain and Trauma, From Darkness to Light.  https://www.abuseincare.org.nz/reports/whanaketia/

Paula Tesoriero, the Chief Executive of Whaikaha – Ministry of Disabled People recorded a video in support of these apologies.  
Paula also wanted to acknowledge the disabled people, tāngata whaikaha Māori, Deaf and tāngata Turi survivors, and outline how Whaikaha can work with government agencies and the community to create change.

Alternate formats of this video can be found on the Whaikaha website: https://www.whaikaha.govt.nz/news/news/message-from-the-chief-executive-of-whaikaha-to-disabled-survivors-of-abuse-in-care
